answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may claim rewards. A registry ties claims to that bond, and independent agents challenge suspicious clusters; if one operator splits into many accounts to farm incentives, proof of shared control or duplicate claims can trigger forfeiture. The rule does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to immobilize capital for every identity and risk losing it. Even at the zenith of demand, a knoll of cheap accounts cannot cross the canyon without paying that cost.
